assessments.reasoning: Section 10.1 defines ordinary named-call focus preservation, and §10.1.1 explicitly permits a context item when the declaration is omitted. The same subsection governs the explicit absent declaration and applies absent focus to both the body and any parameters even when the caller has a focus. The typed declaration and matching-rule paragraphs constrain the interpretation without changing its two named-call branches.

limitations: The absent declaration must be valid. Section 10.1.1 forbids an as attribute on an xsl:context-item with use="absent".
This revision covers named-call focus only. Matching-rule dispatch, initial named-template invocation, other context-item declarations, and type or evaluation failures have separate rules.
